$comment: iOS weaknesses. M2 fills the Mach-O build-hardening half (ios.macho.*): exploit mitigations an iOS binary was or was not compiled with, read by the ios-unpack worker's lief pass and judged by the ios-macho-audit adapter. Severities are deliberately conservative, matching the android native pack: a missing mitigation is not itself a vulnerability, it is a weakened defence that makes an unrelated memory bug more exploitable, so these confirm and rank rather than accuse. maswe_id stays null until verified upstream. M3 (Info.plist and entitlements) adds the ios.ats.*, ios.scheme.*, ios.sharing.* and ios.entitlement.* keys to this same pack.

weaknesses.title: Mach-O is not position-independent
weaknesses.description: The main executable was not linked as a position-independent executable (the MH_PIE flag is clear), so iOS cannot randomise its load address. Without ASLR an attacker knows where the code and its gadgets sit on every launch, which turns a memory-corruption bug into reliable code execution instead of a crash. Every modern Xcode toolchain emits PIE by default, so a non-PIE binary is almost always an old or hand-rolled build.
weaknesses.remediation: Rebuild with position-independent code. In Xcode this is the default; check that the 'Generate Position-Dependent Code' build setting is No and that no linker flag re-enables a fixed base. For a static library or hand-written assembly linked in, pass -Wl,-pie.

weaknesses.title: Mach-O built without stack canaries
weaknesses.description: No stack-protector symbols (___stack_chk_fail / ___stack_chk_guard) are bound in the binary, so functions with on-stack buffers were compiled without the canary that detects a stack overwrite before the function returns. The canary is a cheap, broad mitigation against stack smashing; its absence does not create a bug but removes a guard that would have caught one.
weaknesses.remediation: Rebuild with stack protection. Clang enables -fstack-protector-strong by default for the standard toolchain; confirm no build flag turned it off, and avoid -fno-stack-protector.

weaknesses.title: Mach-O not built with Automatic Reference Counting
weaknesses.description: The binary shows no sign of Automatic Reference Counting (no bound objc_release / objc_retainAutoreleasedReturnValue runtime calls), which means Objective-C memory is managed by hand. Manual retain and release is a common source of use-after-free and double-free bugs, the memory-corruption primitives the other mitigations here only make harder to exploit. Swift and ARC-compiled Objective-C do not have this class of mistake.
weaknesses.remediation: Compile Objective-C sources with ARC (-fobjc-arc, the Xcode default), or move the code to Swift. If a specific file genuinely needs manual memory management, scope -fno-objc-arc to that file rather than the whole target.

weaknesses.title: Mach-O does not enforce non-executable memory
weaknesses.description: The binary opts out of the no-heap-execution protection (the MH_NO_HEAP_EXECUTION or allow-stack-execution disposition), so pages that hold data could also be executed. That removes the W^X guarantee and lets an attacker who can write to memory run what they wrote. This is vanishingly rare on a normal iOS build and usually means a deliberate, dangerous linker setting.
weaknesses.remediation: Remove the linker flag that allows executable data pages (for example -Wl,-allow_stack_execute) and rebuild. There is almost never a legitimate reason for an iOS app to carry it.

weaknesses.title: Mach-O carries no code signature
weaknesses.description: The executable has no LC_CODE_SIGNATURE load command, so the system cannot verify that the binary is intact and from its stated author. A legitimately distributed iOS app is always signed; an unsigned main binary points to a development, re-packaged, or tampered build. It is reported as a resilience and integrity signal, not as a flaw in the app's own logic.
weaknesses.remediation: Ship a properly signed build. If this binary was pulled from a device for analysis the finding is expected; if it represents what users receive, investigate how an unsigned binary came to be distributed.

weaknesses.title: Mach-O is not encrypted
weaknesses.description: The executable has no active FairPlay encryption (its LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO cryptid is 0), so its code can be disassembled directly from the file. App Store distribution applies FairPlay automatically, so a development, enterprise, or sideloaded build is simply not encrypted and the absence here is expected for such a build, not a defect. It is recorded because an unencrypted binary leaves any obfuscation as the only remaining barrier to static analysis.
weaknesses.remediation: No action is required for a non-App-Store build. Where resistance to static analysis matters, do not rely on FairPlay (it protects only the App Store copy); treat the binary as readable and keep secrets and sensitive logic off the device instead.

weaknesses.title: App Transport Security is disabled for the whole app
weaknesses.description: Info.plist sets NSAllowsArbitraryLoads, which switches App Transport Security off for every connection the app makes. ATS is what forces HTTPS with modern TLS; with it off the app may talk to any server over plain HTTP, so traffic can be read and modified on a shared or hostile network. A blanket opt-out is almost never justified, and Apple requires a written justification for it at review.
weaknesses.remediation: Remove NSAllowsArbitraryLoads and let ATS enforce HTTPS. If one or two legacy hosts genuinely cannot do TLS yet, scope the exception to those domains under NSExceptionDomains and keep the global default secure, rather than disabling ATS for everything.

weaknesses.title: App Transport Security is disabled for web content
weaknesses.description: Info.plist sets NSAllowsArbitraryLoadsInWebContent, which lets WKWebView and in-app web views load over plain HTTP even while the rest of the app keeps ATS. Content loaded this way can be tampered with in transit, and a web view often has a bridge back into the app, so injected content is not only a display problem.
weaknesses.remediation: Remove NSAllowsArbitraryLoadsInWebContent and serve web-view content over HTTPS. If specific hosts need an exception, scope it under NSExceptionDomains rather than opening all web content.

weaknesses.title: A named domain is allowed to use cleartext HTTP
weaknesses.description: An NSExceptionDomains entry sets NSExceptionAllowsInsecureHTTPLoads for a specific host, so the app will talk to that host over plain HTTP. Traffic to it can be read and modified on the path. A scoped exception is less sweeping than disabling ATS entirely, but the named host is still an unprotected channel.
weaknesses.remediation: Move the host to HTTPS and remove the exception. If it is a third-party endpoint outside your control, press the provider for TLS; until then treat anything sent to or received from it as public and tamperable.

weaknesses.title: Custom URL scheme can be claimed by another app
weaknesses.description: The app registers a custom URL scheme in CFBundleURLTypes. iOS does not make a scheme exclusive: any other installed app can register the same one, and which app is launched for it is undefined, so a malicious app can intercept links meant for this one, including any data carried in the URL. Input arriving on the scheme is also attacker-controlled and crosses a trust boundary into the app.
weaknesses.remediation: Treat everything arriving on the scheme as untrusted input: validate and authorise it, and never act on a sensitive request (login, payment, token exchange) from a URL alone. For links that must be exclusive to this app, use Universal Links (an associated-domains entitlement backed by an apple-app-site-association file) instead of a custom scheme.

weaknesses.title: The app exposes its Documents directory over file sharing
weaknesses.description: Info.plist sets UIFileSharingEnabled, so the app's Documents directory is reachable over USB through Finder or iTunes, and to anyone with access to an unlocked, trusted computer. Whatever the app writes there (caches, logs, exports, downloaded content) is readable and replaceable without going through the app.
weaknesses.remediation: Turn off UIFileSharingEnabled unless sharing files is a feature users expect. If it is, keep only user documents in that directory and keep tokens, keys, databases and logs elsewhere in the sandbox (Library or the keychain), never under the shared Documents path.

weaknesses.title: The binary is debuggable (get-task-allow)
weaknesses.description: The code-signing entitlements set get-task-allow, which lets a debugger attach to the running process and read or change its memory. This is expected and correct for a development or debug build; on a build that reaches users it is a resilience failure, because anyone with the device can attach to the app, dump its memory and step through its logic. App Store builds have it off.
weaknesses.remediation: Confirm whether this is a development build. If it represents what users receive, ship a Release/distribution build: the App Store and ad-hoc distribution signing turn get-task-allow off, while development signing leaves it on.

weaknesses.title: Keychain access group uses a wildcard
weaknesses.description: A keychain-access-groups entitlement contains a wildcard, which widens the set of apps that can read the keychain items this app stores. Keychain sharing is meant to be scoped to a known group of first-party apps; a wildcard loosens that boundary and can put credentials and keys within reach of code they were not intended for.
weaknesses.remediation: List the exact access groups the app needs to share with, not a wildcard. If the app does not share keychain items with any other app, remove the shared group and let items default to the app's own access group.

weaknesses.title: Associated domains entitlement uses a wildcard
weaknesses.description: An associated-domains entitlement contains a wildcard, so the app accepts Universal Links, and the handoff and shared-credential behaviour that ride on associated domains, from a far wider set of hosts than a named list would. That broadens the surface for links the app will treat as its own and weakens the domain-to-app binding Universal Links exist to provide.
weaknesses.remediation: Name each associated domain explicitly (for example applinks:www.example.com) rather than using a wildcard, and keep the list to the domains the app genuinely owns and serves an apple-app-site-association file from.

weaknesses.title: Backend endpoint addressed over plain HTTP
weaknesses.description: The app carries a plain-HTTP URL for a backend it talks to, found in its resources or binary. This is stronger evidence than a permissive transport policy: the policy says cleartext is allowed, this says the app actually addresses a host over cleartext. Traffic to it can be read and modified by anyone on the network path, and any token, credential or personal data in that exchange is exposed.
weaknesses.remediation: Move the endpoint to TLS and change the URL. Turning on App Transport Security without changing the URL turns a silent interception into an outage, so change both: fix the address and let ATS enforce HTTPS.
